q: When would you fine-tune instead of using RAG?
a: Fine-tune for behaviour: consistent format or style, domain-specific labels (classification, NER), shorter prompts, or a small cheap model for a high-volume narrow task. Use RAG for knowledge that changes or needs citations. They combine well.

Freeze the pretrained weight W and learn a low-rank update ΔW = (α/r)·BA with B (d × r) and A (r × k), r small (4–64). B starts at zero. It trains a tiny fraction of parameters, adapters are a few MB, multiple adapters can share one base model, and BA can be merged into W for zero extra latency.

q: How many trainable parameters does LoRA add to a 4096 × 4096 matrix with r = 8?
a: r(d + k) = 8 × (4096 + 4096) = 65,536, versus 16,777,216 for full fine-tuning: about 0.39%.

LoRA on top of a base model quantised to 4-bit NF4, with double quantisation and paged optimisers. Gradients flow through the frozen 4-bit weights into 16-bit adapters. It lets you fine-tune very large models on a single GPU with little quality loss.

q: How much GPU memory does full fine-tuning of a 7B model need?
a: Roughly 16 bytes per parameter with mixed-precision Adam (weights, gradients, FP32 master copy, two optimiser moments): about 112 GB, plus activations. Inference alone in FP16 needs about 14 GB; in 4-bit about 4 GB.

q: How do you evaluate whether fine-tuning was worth it?
a: Compare against a strong baseline (the base model with a good prompt and few-shot examples, and RAG if relevant) on a held-out task-specific test set, check for regressions in general ability (catastrophic forgetting), and weigh cost and latency.

q: Can fine-tuning reliably teach an LLM new facts?
a: Not reliably. It may memorise some facts but still hallucinate details, can't cite sources, must be retrained when facts change, and can't apply per-user permissions. Use RAG for knowledge and fine-tuning for behaviour, format and style.

q: Why is B initialised to zero in LoRA?
a: So \(BA = 0\) at the start and the adapted model equals the original exactly. Training then moves smoothly from the pretrained behaviour instead of starting from a random perturbation.
Not if you merge it: compute \(W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{r}BA\) once and serve a normal model. Keeping adapters separate adds a small cost but lets one base model serve many adapters.

q: What is catastrophic forgetting and how do you limit it?
a: Fine-tuning erases general abilities the model had. Limit it with LoRA (base frozen), a low learning rate, few epochs, mixing in general data, and evaluating general benchmarks alongside the task metric.
